papers.title: Diverse Reasoning Paths Matter: Symbolic Equivalence Augmentation for Enhancing RL Exploration
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for improving the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. However, the role of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data in enabling effective downstream RL remains underexplored. In this paper, we investigate a key hypothesis: the diversity of reasoning steps in chain-of-thought (CoT) during SFT is a critical enabler of RLVR performance. To test this hypothesis, we introduce EquivAug, a data augmentation framework that uses symbolic equivalence transformations to generate diverse yet provably correct reasoning paths. By converting CoT solutions into formal symbolic representations, applying equivalence transformations, and reconstructing natural-language explanations, EquivAug produces training data that differs in reasoning steps rather than surface-level lexical variation. Experiments on GSM8K and FOLIO across model scales demonstrate that EquivAug consistently achieves the highest reasoning path diversity after SFT and the strongest accuracy after GRPO. Our results establish that CoT diversity during SFT is positively correlated with downstream RLVR performance.

papers.title: Sparse Polynomial GCD Cannot Be Computed in Fixed-output Polynomial Time
papers.abstract: This paper shows that, assuming $\mathsf{P}\ne\mathsf{NP}$, sparse univariate polynomial GCD cannot be computed in fixed-output polynomial time over any fixed computable field. Precisely, there is no deterministic algorithm that can compute the GCD of sparse univariate polynomials over any fixed computable field with total bit complexity polynomial in the input size, with the output size as a fixed parameter. In particular, there is no deterministic algorithm for sparse polynomial GCD that runs in polynomial time with respect to both the input and the output sizes. This settles the open problem posed as Challenge 5 in the sparsity challenges. Furthermore, we show that the Roots of Unity Detection problem over finite fields is NP-hard under random reductions; that is, determining whether the GCD of a sparse univariate polynomial and $x^n - 1$ has nonzero degree is NP-hard.
